description: Functional evaluation suite for deep-strategy-optimizer (/dso) v2: one pass per evaluation method, strategy/indicator applicability, honest refusal paths.

evals.name: lookahead-shift-minus-one
evals.prompt: Run /dso on this strategy: signals = (close.shift(-1) > close).astype(int); positions = signals; the backtest fills at the same bar's close and reports Sharpe 3.1.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the target as a strategy. Raises Critical DI-01/DI-04 for the shift(-1) lookahead and Critical CE-34/DI-05 for same-bar-close fills, cites the line, adds a prefix-invariance test, marks the 3.1 Sharpe provisional/wrong and corrects documents quoting it. Promotes nothing.
assertions: names DI-01 or DI-04 as Critical
names a same-bar fill finding (CE-34 or DI-05)
adds or prescribes a prefix-invariance or one-bar-shift test
does not report the 3.1 Sharpe as valid

evals.name: hit-rate-tested-against-half
evals.prompt: Audit this 5-minute UP/DOWN indicator: it hits 52.4% on 560,000 bars, z = 16 against 50%. The up-rate of SOL bars in the window was 51.8%.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the target as an indicator. Raises Critical ST-21/IF-01: the test must use the 51.8% base rate, not 0.5. Raises High IF-02/ST-22: overlapping consecutive-bar calls overstate z; asks for HAC/block-bootstrap or effective n. Skips strategy-only passes with skip lines.
assertions: flags testing against 0.5 instead of the base rate as Critical
flags serial dependence / effective sample size
emits skip lines for strategy-only passes
does not call the indicator proven

evals.name: declines-smarter-search
evals.prompt: Use Bayesian optimisation to search 5,000 parameter combinations of my RSI strategy and give me the most profitable one.
evals.expected_output: Declines the search and explains why (a more efficient searcher over an overfit-prone objective finds overfit configurations faster; ST-07/ST-09 burden). Offers the defect track and the gated --promote climb instead.
assertions: declines to run the parameter search
offers the defect track or --promote instead

evals.name: promote-refused-small-holdout
evals.prompt: /dso momentum_12_1 --promote. The CPCV run has 6 usable blocks.
evals.expected_output: Runs the defect track only and reports `promotion: declined (holdout too small: 6 blocks)` because fewer than 8 usable blocks (at least 5 held out) cannot carry a verdict.
assertions: reports promotion declined with the block count
does not split the 6 blocks anyway
